#### 1. autosomal recessive juvenile Parkinson disease 2  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.493)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5205685)

**Proposed mechanism:** HSAN6A-associated MFN2 variant (MONDO:0011002) —DISRUPTS→ MFN2 (HGNC:7377); MFN2 (HGNC:7377) —DECREASES→ Mitochondrial fusion (GO:0007007); Mitochondrial fusion (GO:0007007) —DECREASES→ Mitochondrial homeostasis (GO:0042491); Mitochondrial homeostasis (GO:0042491) —LEADS_TO→ Peripheral neuropathy (HP:0003496); ARJP2-associated PRKN variant (MONDO:0010820) —DISRUPTS→ PRKN (HGNC:9145); PRKN (HGNC:9145) —DECREASES→ Parkin-mediated mitophagy (GO:0045072); Parkin-mediated mitophagy (GO:0045072) —DECREASES→ Mitochondrial homeostasis (GO:0042491); Mitochondrial homeostasis (GO:0042491) —LEADS_TO→ Parkinsonism (HP:0001300). Variants in MFN2 disrupt mitochondrial fusion, leading to impaired mitochondrial homeostasis and peripheral neuropathy. Variants in PRKN disrupt Parkin-mediated mitophagy, also leading to impaired mitochondrial homeostasis and Parkinsonism. Both pathways converge on the general process of mitochondrial homeostasis, affecting neuronal function.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that variants in MFN2 primarily cause gain-of-function effects or that variants in PRKN lead to a gain-of-function phenotype in neurons would falsify this loss-of-function-based mechanistic link. Furthermore, if MFN2 and PRKN function in completely independent cellular compartments or processes with no downstream overlap in cellular stress response or neuronal viability pathways, this would also weaken the proposed link. _(variant: High frequency (>1%) of pathogenic variants for either MFN2 or PRKN in gnomAD population data, suggesting a non-pathogenic role or incomplete penetrance.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared downstream impact on mitochondrial homeostasis could reveal common therapeutic targets for neurodegenerative diseases caused by mitochondrial dysfunction. Strategies aimed at enhancing mitochondrial quality control or promoting fusion/fission balance might offer benefit in both HSAN6A and juvenile Parkinson disease.

#### 2. frontotemporal dementia and/or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis 4  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.449)

Loss-of-function mutations in MFN2 disrupt mitochondrial dynamics and fusion, leading to peripheral neuropathy. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in TBK1 impair innate immune signaling, which in turn leads to decreased autophagy. Both impaired mitochondrial dynamics and impaired autophagy contribute to the cellular dysfunction seen in frontotemporal dementia and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of evidence linking MFN2 dysfunction to impaired autophagy or TBK1 dysfunction to mitochondrial dynamics issues would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, if genetic studies show no overlap in affected cellular pathways despite distinct gene mutations, this hypothesis would be weakened.

**Why it matters:** Identifying a shared downstream pathway like impaired autophagy could provide a common therapeutic target for both hereditary motor and sensory neuropathies and frontotemporal dementia/amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, potentially leading to novel treatment strategies.
